title: Oil Filter Housing Quick Drain and Element Change Interval Extension
abstract: Proposal to combine the drain fitting with a quick release housing cover and to extend the filter element change interval, on the basis of oil condition data gathered since the drain nozzle change entered service.

sections.reason: Since the drain change entered service, operators have supplied three years of oil condition data covering roughly two thousand element changes. Element loading at the current interval is consistently below thirty per cent of the design capacity, and the change is now driven by the calendar rather than by condition. Two operators have asked whether the interval can follow the data, and the housing work needed to make the change quick enough to be worth doing at all has been proposed alongside it.
sections.description: The proposal replaces the housing cover with a quick release variant that integrates the drain fitting introduced by the earlier change, so that draining and opening are one action, and replaces the shroud with a lighter profile suited to the new cover. The washer standard at the joint is carried over. The filter element itself is unchanged, which is deliberate: the interval argument rests on the existing element and its existing capacity, and introducing a new element would restart it. Oil pump and pressure sensing are untouched.
sections.effects: Mass reduction of zero point eight kilograms per engine. No electrical load change. Interchangeable with the current standard. If the interval extension is accepted the operator saves one shop visit per engine per two years, which is the entire business case; the housing change on its own does not justify the work.
sections.embodiment_note: Proposal only. Any embodiment would be by retrofit at an engine access opportunity, and the interval change would be a maintenance programme revision rather than an aircraft change.
sections.open_points: The proposal has not been analysed. It needs the oil condition data set validated independently, a position on whether the interval change can be argued without an element requalification, and a decision on whether the housing work should wait for the next planned nacelle standard change.

type_data.production_impact: None proposed; retrofit and maintenance programme change only
